content.text:
Issue [#1374](https://github.com/jdx/usage/issues/1374) is valid. Subcommand names currently cannot receive their own semantic style.

The omission came from [PR #1297](https://github.com/jdx/usage/pull/1297):

- Help styling recognizes `heading`, `option`, and `metavar`.
- The renderer inventories flag and argument spellings before styling rows.
- It does not inventory subcommand names, so command rows fall through as ordinary prose.
- `Style` only selects colored/plain output; there is no configurable theme object today.

Recommended fix:

- Add a `command` semantic style with default bold green, matching the clap example.
- Apply it only to command names—including the synthetic `help` command—not descriptions or command paths in the synopsis.
- Preserve byte-identical plain output.

This is mechanically straightforward but touches several parity surfaces:

- Both Rust renderers (`usage-lib` and `usage-argv`)
- The derive-time style validator
- The shared style corpus and conformance tests
- Go’s accepted template vocabulary, although Go output remains plain
- Help-template documentation

Tests should cover custom command headings, hidden commands, `disable_help_subcommand`, aliases, wrapped/next-line help, and ANSI-stripped output.

One nuance: adding `{$command}` creates a distinct semantic token with a default color, but it does not create a user-configurable palette. A true theme API would be a separate, larger feature. I recommend the semantic token as the focused resolution.

No files were changed. The active checkout is detached at an older commit, so I inspected the current local `main` ref without disturbing the existing dirty worktree.
